claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you a few more questions about Alex to assess your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school anymore. He's actually started an apprenticeship up in Aberdeen - he moved up there to do it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a couple more questions about Alex's apprenticeship to make a proper assessment.

**Is this an apprenticeship in England, or is it specifically in Scotland since he's in Aberdeen?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's in Scotland - he's doing it in Aberdeen, so that's where he is now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**When did Alex start this apprenticeship in Scotland?** (I'm asking because there are different rules depending on timing and circumstances.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He just started it recently - within the last few weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**How many hours per week is Alex working in his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact hours, to be honest. It's a proper apprenticeship though, so I imagine it's full-time during the week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One final question:

**Before Alex started the apprenticeship, were you receiving Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's what I'm trying to find out now - whether I'm eligible to claim it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you would be ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Under the Child Benefit rules, you stop being eligible if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training. Since Alex is 17, has left education, and has started what you describe as a full-time apprenticeship (which typically involves 30+ hours of work per week), this means he would be working more than the 24-hour threshold.

While the rules specifically mention that starting an apprenticeship in England disqualifies a child, Alex's full-time apprenticeship in Scotland would still disqualify him under the more general rule about paid work of 24+ hours per week when no longer in approved education.

If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's circumstances change in the future, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
